item.title: Rosso’s Immigration legacy: Passport backlog cleared, borders strengthened
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso has left the Immigration and Border Security Ministry after delivering major reforms, which include clearing the passport backlog, expanding immigration services across the country and introducing new digital systems. Mr Rosso officially handed over the ministry to the new Minister for Immigration, William Bando, on Wednesday, July 22.
item.content:encoded:
Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso has left the Immigration and Border Security Ministry after delivering major reforms, which include clearing the passport backlog, expanding immigration services across the country and introducing new digital systems.

Mr Rosso officially handed over the ministry to the new Minister for Immigration, William Bando, on Wednesday, July 22.

When Rosso took over Immigration ministry in October 2022, one of the biggest challenges was the large number of delayed passport applications and a shortage of passport books caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

He said the government worked with the passport manufacturer to secure more passport books and speed up processing.

“Today, there is no backlog,” Mr Rosso said.

During his three years and nine months, Mr Rosso said the authority had made major improvements.

“We’ve accomplished a great deal in a short time. We’re not where we want to be yet, but we’re certainly not where we used to be,” he said.

Under his leadership, ICSA set up offices in Mt Hagen and Kokopo to provide regional services. New offices were also established in Arawa, Motukea International Sea Port, Rabaul Sea Port, Kiunga, Tabubil and Nadzab Tomodachi International Airport in Lae.

Mr Rosso said the opening of the Passport Printing Office at the Momase Regional Office in Lae was one of the key achievements of his term.

He said people from the Momase region, Highlands and parts of the New Guinea Islands could now access passport services closer to home instead of travelling to Port Moresby.

ICSA also improved visa services by reintroducing visa auto-grant processing, expanding online visa applications and increasing Visa-on-Arrival access for more countries.

Mr Rosso said these changes helped promote tourism, trade and investment in Papua New Guinea.

The authority also strengthened its international services, with migration officers appointed to PNG diplomatic missions in countries including China, Australia, Malaysia, Indonesia, India and the Philippines.

Mr Rosso highlighted technology upgrades as another major achievement, including the introduction of the new PNG e-passport with improved security features in 2025.

ICSA also launched the Sponsor Portal, allowing companies to apply online for work permits and working resident visas.

The introduction of the PNG Digital Arrival Card replaced the old paper arrival card, allowing travellers to complete arrival information online before travelling.

The Immigration Operations Command Centre was also established in Port Moresby in 2025 to strengthen immigration intelligence and border monitoring.

Mr Rosso also took a tough approach against foreigners who breached PNG’s immigration laws.

He said more than 500 illegal foreign nationals had been removed from the country during his time as minister for activities including illegal work, illegal businesses and other breaches of visa conditions.

“We welcome foreigners and their business, trade and investment to PNG, but they must follow our laws,” he said.

Mr Rosso also re-established the Citizenship Advisory Committee to address delays in citizenship applications.

The committee helped clear a backlog of applications, including cases involving West Papuans who have lived in PNG for many years.

He also directed a review of immigration laws, including the Citizenship Act, to address issues affecting Papua New Guineans who lost citizenship while working or studying overseas.

Mr Rosso thanked Chief Migration Officer Wellington Navasivu, senior officers and all ICSA staff for their support during his time as minister.

With Mr Bando now taking over the ministry, he inherits an immigration authority that has undergone major changes in services, technology and border management under Mr Rosso’s leadership.

item.title: Solo triumphs in penalty shoot out to qualify for U17 World Cup
item.description: The Solomon Islands have qualified for FIFA U-17 World Cup 2027, coming from behind to defeat Papua New Guinea on penalties at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby. Henry Fa'arodo's side found themselves on the back foot for long stages of their third place play-off at OFC U-16 Men's Championship 2026, but found a way to rescue victory from the jaws of defeat, ripping a World Cup spot away fro
item.content:encoded:
The Solomon Islands have qualified for FIFA U-17 World Cup 2027, coming from behind to defeat Papua New Guinea on penalties at the PNG Football Stadium in Port Moresby.

Henry Fa'arodo's side found themselves on the back foot for long stages of their third place play-off at OFC U-16 Men's Championship 2026, but found a way to rescue victory from the jaws of defeat, ripping a World Cup spot away from Papua New Guinea with a late equaliser and four classy spot kicks in the penalty shootout.

The win sends the Solomon Islands through to their second FIFA U-17 World Cup, and their first in eight years, after previously qualifying for the tournament in 2019. It is also their highest finish at an OFC U-16 Men's Championship since hosting the competition in 2018.

It was Papua New Guinea and their striker Boas Tommy who spurned the best chances of a goalless first half. Twice Tommy fluffed his lines, almost running straight into the waiting arms of goalkeeper Eddie Aefi after being played in-behind.

Attempting to qualify for a maiden FIFA U-17 World Cup, the nerves were evident from the tournament hosts. They had the woodwork in their way when a long-raking free kick delivery ricocheted off the crossbar with the help of the gloves of Aefi, before defender Bomecge Basananuc had a header cleared off the goal-line from the following corner.

Ultimately the pressure told though, and it was captain Matthew Sopo who provided the breakthrough for Papua New Guinea in the 66th minute. The midfielder was first to pounce on a loose ball at the top of the box, driving a superb first-time effort into the top-left corner of the net on his right foot.

It looked as Sopo’s goal might prove decisive, but despite having been outplayed for the majority of the contest, the Solomon Islands mustered a miraculous equaliser to send the third place play-off to a penalty shoot-out with six minutes of normal time to play. PNG goalkeeper Luther Rodney failed to keep hold of a routine delivery in the box, allowing Andriano Kabolo to scramble the ball into the goal in the 84th minute.

The Solomon Islands had lost on penalties to Fiji in the semi-final, but held their nerve better on this occasion, profiting on two missed spot kicks from Papua New Guinea to book their World Cup tickets.

George Lea'i slotted the winning penalty, sparking emotional scenes on both sides, as Papua New Guinea fell crestfallen whilst those in Solomon Islands colours celebrated their place at the World Cup in Qatar next year.

item.title: Child among three dead, five still missing in Milne Bay dinghy tragedy
item.description: Details surrounding the dinghy mishap in Milne Bay Province are slowly emerging Reports received from Tarakwaruru Sub-Health Center in Makamaka Rural Local Level Government indicate that a seven-year-old was among the three people found dead, and not four as reported earlier.
item.content:encoded:
Details surrounding the dinghy mishap in Milne Bay Province are slowly emerging

Reports received from Tarakwaruru Sub-Health Center in Makamaka Rural Local Level Government indicate that a seven-year-old was among the three people found dead, and not four as reported earlier.

A two-year-old is among the five people still missing at sea.

Leo Rere, a nursing officer at Tarakwaruru Sub-Health Center who is assisting in the search and rescue mission, said a seven-year-old girl was among the three female bodies recovered.

The bodies were all found on the beachfront at Wabubu Village, with the seven-year-old girl still lifelessly clinging to her mother.

Recounting the ordeal based on the skipper's account, Mr Rere said the two-year-old boy was swept off the dinghy by strong waves before it capsized. His body has not yet been recovered.

The skipper also confirmed that the total number of people onboard was thirteen [13], and not ten as reported earlier.

Apart from the skipper, who swam ashore to seek help, the other three survivors clung to the capsized dinghy until assistance arrived between 8 and 9pm.

Meanwhile, Milne Bay Provincial Disaster Coordinator Randall Ganisi said two dinghies from Tarakwaruru were deployed to assist in the search and rescue operation at the time of the tragedy.

A separate dinghy carrying two police officers was sent yesterday [Friday] with fuel supplies to support the search efforts.

Villages along the coast of Makamaka RLLG have been alerted to look out for any of the missing persons and report any sightings to the authorities.

item.title: Boxer James Paul advances as Team PNG reps nation in Scotland

Meanwhile, in the Women’s 60kg, female boxer Petronella Nokenoke represented with heart and determination in the Women's 60kg Round of 16 and the contest ended in favor
item.content:encoded:
Competition at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow is underway with James Paul advancing to the next round of the Men's 65kg boxing competition with 3-2 points win over Rashield Williams of Bahamas in the Round of 32 last night.

Meanwhile, in the Women’s 60kg, female boxer Petronella Nokenoke represented with heart and determination in the Women's 60kg Round of 16 and the contest ended in favor of England's Lucy Kings-Wheatley [5-0] Win on Points].

Swimming was also featured yesterday in day one of competition with PNG swim team’s four Commonwealth Games debutants competing in the Women’s 50 meters Butterfly and the Men’s 100 meters Breaststroke

In the Women’s 50m Butterfly, 18 year old Joanna Chen 15 year old and Roxanne Kirarock both recorded new Personal Bests, clocking 31.90s and 32.25s respectively.

17 year old Jhnayali Tokome-Garap produced an outstanding swim of 30.29s to set a new Papua New Guinea National Record for the 17-year-old age group, breaking the previous record that had stood since the 2014 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

In the Men’s 100m Breaststroke, Thomas Chen won his heat with a time of 1:09.87s, recording his fastest swim of the 2026 season.

item.content:encoded:
Member for Samurai Murua Henry Isi Leonard has called on the Government to hold large emitters of greenhouse gases responsible for the rapid increase in natural disasters faced in the country.

Leonard cited the recent Tropical Cyclone Maila which hit Milne Bay’s Budi Budi and Woodlark islands, adding its now being coupled with the intensifying El Nino, resulting in water shortages among other severe impacts.

The Member for Samarai Murua also highlighted the need for a national shipping policy.

He says presently, the shipping industry is monopolized, with huge costs being passed onto consumers.

item.title: Australian High Commissioner joins PM on official visit to Hela Province
item.description: Australian High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea, His Excellency Ewen McDonald, joined Prime Minister James Marape on a joint official visit to Hela Province on Friday. The delegation inspected several key infrastructure and development sites across the province, including a tour of the PNG LNG Project facility at Nogoli.
item.content:encoded:
Australian High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea, His Excellency Ewen McDonald, joined Prime Minister James Marape on a joint official visit to Hela Province on Friday.

The delegation inspected several key infrastructure and development sites across the province, including a tour of the PNG LNG Project facility at Nogoli.

The visit concluded with a summit between the leaders and public servants from the Hela Provincial Administration and the Tari-Pori District Administration.

Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu formally welcomed High Commissioner McDonald and briefed the delegation on the province’s development progress, achievements, and challenges since gaining administrative autonomy in 2012.

Mr. Angu highlighted major reforms within the public service, noting that issues such as absenteeism, poor dress standards, and lack of punctuality have been addressed. He said a new culture of accountability, discipline, and professionalism is now in place.

Drawing on his own experience in public service, High Commissioner McDonald commended the reforms and stressed the responsibility of government workers.

“As a public servant myself, I deeply understand the weight of responsibility we carry,” Mr. McDonald said. “Together, we must live up to our calling as servants of the people. Our priority is to ensure essential services reach those who need them most.

Mr. McDonald also congratulated public servants and reaffirmed Australia’s commitment to partnering with PNG on service delivery and development.

Prime Minister Marape said progress in Hela and across PNG depends on strong collaboration.

“Sustainable development requires partnership between the National Government, our international development partners, and provincial administrations,” Marape said.

“That is how we will deliver real change for the people of Hela and for all of Papua New Guinea.”

item.content:encoded:
‎‎ A dinghy ferrying passengers to Cape Vogel village of Makamaka LLG in Alotau District, overturned yesterday afternoon while crossing from Girumia point to Sibiribiri in Milne Bay Province.

‎Details surrounding the incident are still sketchy. However, Makamaka LLG president, Lloyd Franklin, in a text message to NBC news, said a dinghy carrying ten people overturned at around 5:30pm on on Thursday, while crossing from Girumia Point in Weraura LLG to Sibiribiri Point in Makamaka LLG, Alotau District. ‎ ‎Franklin said among the ten, three adults - two male and one female survived the incident. ‎Four females - a student and three adults have been confirmed dead while three adults -a female and two males are still missing. ‎ ‎He said the four deceased were transported on Friday evening to Baiawa Village, Makamaka LLG.

item.title: Long neglected Kotna–Rulna Road upgrade restores hope
item.description: For many years, the people living along the Kotna-Rulna Road in Dei District, Western Highlands Province, have been cut off from basic government services because of poor road access.
